newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open lower on profit-taking.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Friday as profit-taking trimmed some of the market's recent gains, analysts said.
U.S. trade figures for May, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, is the main piece of economic news that the market is due to receive during the trading session.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, that the trade deficit widened in May to $9.18 billion versus $8.36 billion in April due to both slower export growth than at the start of the year and to another solid increase in imports.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 7/32 to 101-17/32, yielding 6.51 percent.
Ten-year notes were down 6/32 to 102-30/32, yielding 6.22 percent.
Five-year notes were down 3/32 to 100-17/32, yielding 6.12 percent and two-year notes were down 1/32 to 100-7/32, yielding 5.88 percent.
At the short end of the maturity curve, three- and six-month bills were unchanged at 5.08 percent and 5.11 percent, respectively. Year bill rates were up three basis points to 5.25 percent.
Analysts said a May trade gap of $9.2 billion would not really impact the bond market.
But they said the profit-taking that began late Thursday and sent prices lower early Friday was likely to continue.
"The market is ripe for more profit-taking," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A.
Stiles said options expirations at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT could offer some interest.
"What's interesting is what's going to happen with options expirations since we had so much activity with the 115-00 call earlier this week," he said.

Referring to a large purchase of 115 calls early this week, Stiles said, "It was big so therefore I can't rule out another try at 115, but with the September bond contract opening at 114-10, they've got a lot of work to do."

Stiles said participants were taking profits ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday and auctions of two- and five-year notes on Tuesday and Wednesday, respectively.
"You have Greenspan and supply," he said. "It's not complicated."
Stiles said there was "a lot of profit-taking" in 10-year notes which have been outperformers.
The market will also get the University of Michigan preliminary July consumer sentiment index, forecast at 104.6 versus 104.5 previously.
But that need not hurt the market, Stiles said.
"Consumer confidence is at cyclical highs but that will only jar the market when it translates into spending, and it wil take a while to see if it does," he said.
